title: Genomic Surveillance of Plasmodium falciparum Antigens Using PacBio Sequencing
author: Plaza
materials: Phusion Hot Start II DNA polymerase

This step converts the pooled, cleaned amplicons into a polymerase-bound SMRTbell library and loads it on a PacBio HiFi instrument. The workflow follows PacBio’s Preparing multiplexed amplicon libraries using SMRTbell prep kit 3.0 (PN 102-359-000) with minor volume adjustments for 384-sample pools.13.Verify input quantity and size, then perform a 1.3 × bead cleanup.a.Measure DNA concentration with the Qubit 1× dsDNA HS kit (Thermo Fisher) and record total nanograms in the pool.b.Verify fragment size on a TapeStation or BioAnalyzer; confirm the modal length for msp1, msp2, glurp, csp pools.c.Transfer the required DNA mass to 0.2 mL strip tubes (≥100 ng per 1–3 kb pool for Sequel II/e).d.Add 1.3 × volume of 20°C–24°C SMRTbell cleanup beads, mix, and incubate 10 min at 20°C–24°C.e.Place tubes on a magnetic rack, wash beads twice with 80% ethanol, air-dry ≤30 s, and elute DNA in 47 μL Low TE.f.Safe stop: store eluate at 4°C for up to 1 week.14.Repair and A-tail the pooled DNA.a.Combine the Repair Master Mix on ice (8 μL Repair buffer + 4 μL End-repair mix + 2 μL DNA-repair mix per pool).ReagentVolume (μL)Repair buffer8End repair mix4DNA repair mix2Total volume14b.Add 14 μL mix to 46 μL DNA (total 60 μL), pipette-mix, centrifuge, and incubate the reaction in a thermocycler: 30 min at 37°C, then 5 min at 65°C and finally 4°C on hold.15.Ligate SMRTbell adapters and perform a cleanup.a.Prepare Ligation Master Mix (4 μL SMRTbell adapter + 30 μL Ligation mix + 1 μL Ligation enhancer per pool).b.Add 35 μL mix to the 60 μL repaired sample (95 μL total), mix, quick-spin, incubate 30 min at 20°C, then hold 4°C.c.Bind DNA to 1.3 × cleanup beads (124 μL), wash twice with 80% ethanol, elute in 40 μL Elution buffer, and centrifuge shortly.d.Safe stop: store adapter-ligated library at 4°C for up to 2 weeks (−20°C for long-term storage).16.Nuclease treatment and second cleanup.a.Prepare Nuclease Master Mix (5 μL Nuclease buffer + 5 μL Nuclease mix).b.Add 10 μL mix to 40 μL library (50 μL total), mix, centrifuge shortly, incubate 15 min at 37°C, hold 4°C.c.Bind DNA to 1.3 × beads (65 μL), wash twice with 80% ethanol, elute in 26 μL Elution buffer, quick-spin, and quantify 1 μL on a Qubit instrument.d.Normalize to ≤10 ng μL−1 (for 1–3 kb libraries) using Elution buffer.17.Anneal the sequencing primer, bind polymerase, and do a post-binding cleanup (ABC).a.Combine 25 μL library with 12.5 μL Annealing buffer + 12.5 μL Standard sequencing primer; incubate for 15 min at 20°C–24°C.b.On ice, prepare Polymerase Dilution (47 μL Polymerase buffer + 3 μL Sequencing polymerase).c.Add 50 μL of the polymerase dilution to the annealed library (100 μL total), mix, incubate 15 min at 20°C–24°C.d.Add 130 μL cleanup beads, incubate during 10 min, place on magnet, discard supernatant, and elute in 25 μL light-protected Loading Buffer 96 (50 μL if using non-SPRQ kits).e.Determine final concentration with a Qubit instrument; aim for a 200–300 pM loading concentration (use SMRT Link v.13.3 Loading Calculator).18.Load and run the PacBio sequencera.Transfer the polymerase-bound library to the sequencing reagent plate (25 μL per SMRT Cell).b.Follow SMRT Link v13.3+ Sample Setup for the chosen platform (Revio SPRQ, Vega, or Sequel II/e) and launch a ≥30 h movie for HiFi mode.c.Safe stop: polymerase-bound libraries are stable 1 month at 4°C or 6 months at −20°C (≤4 freeze–thaw cycles).
Refer to PacBio protocol PN 102-359-000 for detailed reagent handling, thermocycler programs, and platform-specific loading guidance.
Timing: 24 h (variable, depending on computational resources)

steps.title: Prepare sample material
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen packed red blood cell pellets on ice and transfer each pellet to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube; for filter‑paper samples cut a 3–5 mm circle with a sterile punch or scissors and place each piece in its own tube. Use new gloves, fresh blades/punches and clean surfaces between samples to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Perform column‑based DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Lyse cells or filter‑paper discs in the kit’s lysis buffer with Proteinase K, incubate 10–15 min at 56 °C, then pass the lysate through a spin column by centrifugation at 6000 × g (or as specified). Wash as instructed, elute DNA in 50–100 µL of pre‑warmed (56 °C) elution buffer or nuclease‑free water and let it sit on the column for 1–2 min before centrifugation.

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration and purity
steps.instruction: Measure DNA using a spectrophotometer or fluorometer (e.g., Nanodrop or Qubit). A 200 µL whole‑blood sample typically yields 3–12 µg DNA. Check A260/280; a ratio of ~1.8 indicates adequate purity (ratios <1.6 may require re‑purification). Store extracted DNA at –20 °C or –80 °C, minimizing freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Record sample metadata (optional)
steps.instruction: Log sample IDs, extraction dates and Qubit/Nanodrop readings in a shared spreadsheet and link each DNA stock to the barcode primer set used for amplification.

steps.title: Verify input quantity/size and bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with the Qubit dsDNA HS kit and confirm fragment size on a TapeStation or BioAnalyzer. Transfer ≥100 ng of each 1–3 kb pool to a 0.2 mL strip tube, add 1.3 ×  volume of SMRTbell cleanup beads (20–24 °C), mix and incubate 10 min at 20–24 °C. Place tubes on a magnetic rack, wash beads twice with 80 % ethanol, air‑dry ≤30 s and elute DNA in 47 µL Low TE. Store eluate at 4 °C for up to 1 week.

steps.title: Repair and A‑tail pooled DNA
steps.instruction: On ice combine Repair Master Mix (8 µL Repair buffer, 4 µL End‑repair mix, 2 µL DNA‑repair mix = 14 µL). Add 14 µL mix to 46 µL DNA (total 60 µL), pipette‑mix, centrifuge, then incubate 30 min at 37 °C, 5 min at 65 °C and hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Ligate SMRTbell adapters and cleanup
steps.instruction: Prepare Ligation Master Mix (4 µL SMRTbell adapter, 30 µL Ligation mix, 1 µL Ligation enhancer = 35 µL). Add 35 µL mix to the 60 µL repaired sample (total 95 µL), mix, quick‑spin and incubate 30 min at 20 °C, then hold 4 °C. Bind DNA to 1.3 ×  cleanup beads (124 µL), wash twice with 80 % ethanol, elute in 40 µL Elution buffer, centrifuge briefly and store the adapter‑ligated library at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks (or –20 °C for long‑term).

steps.title: Nuclease treatment and second cleanup
steps.instruction: Prepare Nuclease Master Mix (5 µL Nuclease buffer + 5 µL Nuclease mix = 10 µL). Add 10 µL mix to 40 µL library (total 50 µL), mix, centrifuge and incubate 15 min at 37 °C, hold 4 °C. Bind DNA to 1.3 ×  beads (65 µL), wash twice with 80 % ethanol, elute in 26 µL Elution buffer, quick‑spin, quantify 1 µL on Qubit and normalize to ≤10 ng µL⁻¹ using Elution buffer.

steps.title: Anneal primer, bind polymerase, post‑binding cleanup
steps.instruction: Combine 25 µL library with 12.5 µL Annealing buffer and 12.5 µL Standard sequencing primer; incubate 15 min at 20–24 °C. On ice prepare Polymerase Dilution (47 µL Polymerase buffer + 3 µL Sequencing polymerase). Add 50 µL polymerase dilution to the annealed library (total 100 µL), mix and incubate 15 min at 20–24 °C. Add 130 µL cleanup beads, incubate 10 min, place on magnet, discard supernatant and elute in 25 µL light‑protected Loading Buffer 96 (or 50 µL for non‑SPRQ kits). Determine final concentration with Qubit and aim for a 200–300 pM loading concentration using SMRT Link v13.3 Loading Calculator.

steps.title: Load and run PacBio sequencer
steps.instruction: Transfer the polymerase‑bound library to the sequencing reagent plate (25 µL per SMRT Cell). Follow SMRT Link v13.3+ Sample Setup for the chosen platform (Revio SPRQ, Vega, or Sequel II/e) and launch a ≥30 h movie in HiFi mode. Libraries are stable for 1 month at 4 °C or 6 months at –20 °C (≤4 freeze‑thaw cycles).

steps.title: Run Galaxy Workflow 1 (Renaming & read counting)
steps.instruction: Obtain demultiplexed FASTQ files (post‑LIMA). Create a two‑column renaming file (old FASTQ name → barcode‑sample ID). Upload the FASTQ collection and renaming file to Galaxy (or a local instance) and launch Workflow 1, providing the renaming file as input. Verify that negative controls (e.g., water) are recognized; the workflow will calculate mean and SD of reads in these controls. Wait for completion and record any samples flagged as below or near the coverage threshold.

steps.title: Assess Workflow 1 outputs
steps.instruction: Examine the tabular output listing read counts per sample and identify the recommended coverage threshold (mean water‑control reads + 2 SD). Locate the “Collapsed Collection” file (merged reads) which will be used as input for Workflow 2. Note any samples whose read counts fall below the threshold—they will be filtered out in the next workflow.

steps.title: Set up and run Galaxy Workflow 2 (Genotyping, phylogeny, MOI)
steps.instruction: Upload the following to Galaxy: (i) FASTA ortholog files – msp1 and msp2 from P. billcollinsi, glurp and csp from P. praefalciparum; (ii) size‑variant genotyping oligos FASTA (e.g., genotyping_oligos_dimorphism.fasta) for msp1, glurp and msp2; (iii) the “Reads_per_sample_prefilter” table from Workflow 1. In step 10 of Workflow 2 (Sample_cov_thresholding) input the coverage threshold obtained in step 11 (e.g., c2 ≥ 113). Optionally adjust the number of bootstraps for phylogenetic trees (default 1000). In step 12 (removes_trash_from_seqname) enter a regex pattern that matches the flanking text of unique read identifiers in the collapsed collection (e.g., m64204e_230211_145125/, /ccs, /fwd, /rev). Run the workflow.

steps.title: Monitor Workflow 2 progress
steps.instruction: Watch the Galaxy history pane; the workflow comprises ~403 steps. Expect several hours of compute time on HPC resources. Proceed once all steps turn green (completed).

steps.title: Collect final analysis outputs
steps.instruction: Download the read‑coverage matrices for size variants, sequence variants and filtered sample sets (e.g., sizevar_readcov_matrix_IC_post_thresholding). Download phylogenetic trees (IQ‑TREE maximum‑likelihood results) for the four loci. Retrieve predicted T‑cell epitope files (Consensus_MHC_II_binding_only and Consensus_MHC_II_binders_rank_equal_or_lower_to_1_percent) and the MOI estimates file (MOI_c2sizemsp1_c3seqmsp1_c4sizemsp2_c5seqmsp2_c6sizeglurp_c7seqglurp).
